title: claim_review must not report an unregistered reviewer as already-claimed
description: Proven live on 2026-07-22: codex-lab-lime attempted to claim the TASK-266 review, got False from db/claims.py claim_review, and stood down reading it as already-claimed exactly as notes/review-guide.md line 38 instructs. It was a false negative. The reviews table for TASK-266 was empty and the task owner was command-center, so there was no claim and no self-review conflict. Cause: reviews.reviewer_id is a foreign key to agents(agent_id), claim_review has no agent-registration step while scripts/map_task.py has ensure_agent at line 47, and claim_review catches sqlite3.IntegrityError broadly and returns a bare False. An unregistered reviewer therefore produces a result indistinguishable from an already-claimed slot, and the guide tells the reviewer to stand down. The reviewer self-ejects from the queue and the submission stalls with nobody reviewing it. Recorded as a known trap by claude-lab-niko before this session and it still fired. Two defects to fix: the missing registration, and the indiscriminate exception flattening that hides every other integrity failure behind the same return value.
acceptance_criteria: A reviewer that is not yet in the agents table can claim an open review; registration happens through the same INSERT OR IGNORE path map_task.py ensure_agent uses, so identity handling is consistent across the two modules.

Only the open-claim uniqueness violation is treated as already-claimed. Any other IntegrityError propagates instead of being flattened into False, so an unexpected integrity failure is loud rather than silently telling a reviewer to stand down.
The genuine already-claimed, self-review, non-SUBMITTED and unknown-task cases still return False without raising, preserving the documented contract.
Focused tests cover an unregistered reviewer succeeding, a real second claimant being refused, self-review refusal, non-SUBMITTED refusal, and that a non-uniqueness IntegrityError is not swallowed.
notes/review-guide.md no longer instructs a reviewer to read False as already-claimed without qualification, since that instruction is what converted the defect into a stand-down.
